rationale: A wins because it keeps the story shapes hard and treats missing proof as a gate, not confetti: "at least one named publisher enrolled in the program" and "a real (even rough) dollar figure" are exactly the questions a media-business reporter will ask. B has real instincts, but "The publishers threatening Perplexity with lawsuits are the same ones it's now offering to pay" overstates the record, and "the receipts its last valuation is betting on" turns a thin valuation fact into investor fan fiction.
gaps_in_A: It is too quick to refuse "The publisher-payout angle: how much will publishers actually earn?" The undisclosed-payout fact can be its own opacity story if paired with publisher reaction or comparable AI-publisher deals.

The shopping angle leans on a broad trend line, "where does commerce happen next," without any supplied evidence that retail reporters are already tracking that frame. Keep it, but make the proof do more work.
It buries a potentially useful retail data angle inside proof: "query volume that actually converts to revenue" could have been its own sharper channel-size story.
gaps_in_B: "The publishers threatening Perplexity with lawsuits are the same ones it's now offering to pay" is too confident. The update says Perplexity has faced legal threats and is offering a publisher program; it does not prove the threatened publishers are participating or even targeted.

"subscription revenue alone hasn't proven out for AI answer engines" may be plausible market context, but it is not in the supplied facts. That is how smart-sounding unsupported claims sneak into bad pitches.

"Perplexity's new revenue streams are the receipts its last valuation is betting on" invents an investor thesis from a valuation mention. Without an investor quote or funding details, that angle is a question, not a headline.
The first angle's proof, "company comment on strategy," is too soft. A monetization story needs fee structure, revenue-share mechanics, and materiality, not another executive quote about strategy.
